messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression in today's canary. Host-side parse + tokenize CPU at P50 is up ~8-12% under a 2k QPS workload.

sam: Repro steps? commit/region?

maya: Canary: us-west-2, commit 0f3d9a2. Baseline load generator same as yesterday. Perf shows hotspots in parse_stream() and Tokenizer::normalize.

jordan: Can you drop a flame graph or pprof sample?

maya: Quick perf top snippet from the canary box:
```
# top functions
parse_stream                      34.1%
Tokenizer::normalize              22.4%
http2::inflate_headers            8.9%
grpc::reader::read                6.7%
writev                           4.5%
```

sam: Hm — writev shows up but not huge. Any change to the proxy or small-write coalescing recently?

jordan: I pushed a micro-optimization to proxy last week to reduce buffer latency; it changed iovec grouping in edge path. Could be causing more syscalls for minibatches.

maya: Interesting — KV cache hit rate is flat, but average effective batch size dropped from 4 -> 2 under same load. That would explain more per-request overhead.

sam: If batching heuristics are misfiring we should capture the decision trace. Add BATCH_TRACE and record batch sizes / decision reasons. Also capture chunk-size histogram on ingress.

jordan: I can revert the iovec grouping locally and run the canary. Quick experiment showed revert reduces parse_stream CPU by ~6% on a small replay.

maya: Good. I'll schedule a canary with proxy revert + a kernel-selection hint that favors larger coalesces. Also want to try a tokenizer micro-fix to avoid an extra allocation in normalize.

sam: For the tokenizer change, prefer a zero-copy view (string_ref) for ascii-normalization where possible. That should cut Tokenizer::normalize by ~10-20% on short inputs.

maya: PR up: reduce-copy-tokenizer (https://git/repo/p/r/123). Running microbench now.

jordan: Also instrument grpc stream framing: an edge change in chunking logic may produce many ~128B frames instead of 1-2KB frames. That amplifies header inflation cost. Add histogram for frame sizes.

maya: Added frame-size histogram to canary (enabled via env). Early telemetry shows a new mode around 180B frames that wasn't present before.

sam: That matches small-batch tail behavior — batching heuristics + proxy change = fragmentation. Two levers: revert proxy grouping OR adjust batching heuristics to delay until we reach larger aggregate.

jordan: If revert helps, we should later harden batching heuristics: prefer batching until either token-count threshold OR time budget, whichever yields >1.5KB aggregate. Add unit test with synthetic small requests.

maya: Ops: scheduling the revert canary now.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled — canary-revert-proxy at 6172034580 by jordan

sam: After the canary, please share pprof and batch traces. If CPU drop is confirmed, follow-up tasks: (1) permanent revert + smaller rollback PR for proxy, (2) tokenizer zero-copy merge, (3) add regression test for batching heuristic, (4) add streaming frame-size alert.

maya: Will do. If revert doesn't fully fix it, next step is a deeper KV-caching timeline trace to see if cache warm paths changed ordering.

jordan: Agree. Also we should add a short-lived perf test to CI that runs on a small replay to catch this class of regression early.

maya: I'll post pprof + batch traces once canary completes (ETA ~2h). Thanks team. :thumbsup:
